title: Executive Summary of The Third Report of The National Cholesterol Education Program (NCEP) Expert Panel on Detection, Evaluation, And Treatment of High Blood Cholesterol In Adults (Adult Treatment Panel III)
authors: Expert Panel on Detection, Evaluation, and Treatment of High Blood Cholesterol in Adults
journal: JAMA; also National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, NIH Publication No. 01-3670, May 2001
funder: not stated; the report is issued by the National Cholesterol Education Program of the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute
authorConflicts: The executive summary lists panel members (chair S.M. Grundy) without declarations of financial relationships.
result: ATP I (1988) targeted primary prevention in people with LDL cholesterol of 160 mg/dL or more, or 130 to 159 mg/dL with 2 or more risk factors; ATP II set an LDL goal of 100 mg/dL or less in coronary heart disease. ATP III classifies LDL cholesterol below 100 mg/dL as optimal, 100 to 129 near optimal, 130 to 159 borderline high, 160 to 189 high and 190 or more very high; total cholesterol below 200 mg/dL desirable, 200 to 239 borderline high and 240 or more high. It made diabetes a coronary heart disease risk equivalent and used Framingham 10-year risk. Drug therapy is considered at LDL 130 mg/dL or more for coronary heart disease or equivalents (10-year risk above 20%; goal below 100), at 130 or more for 2 or more risk factors with 10-year risk 10 to 20% and 160 or more with risk below 10% (goal below 130), and at 190 or more for 0 to 1 risk factor (goal below 160; drug optional at 160 to 189).
